bibliographic.title: DLT Compliance Reporting
bibliographic.authors: Henrik Axelsen; Johannes Rude Jensen; Omri Ross
bibliographic.citation_apa: Axelsen, H., Jensen, J. R., & Ross, O. (unclear). DLT Compliance Reporting [Research in progress]. University of Copenhagen / eToroX Labs.

methodology.study_design: Design, development, and evaluation of a DLT artefact for automated collection and enrichment of transactional compliance data, conducted with industry and regulatory representatives
methodology.sample_description: Group of representatives from industry and regulatory authorities
methodology.sector: financial services; banking; regulatory compliance reporting
methodology.technology_context: Distributed ledger technology (DLT) for ITS risk compliance reporting automation via a pull-model; not LLM, conversational AI, chatbots, agents, or RAG

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The study addresses DLT-based compliance reporting automation in banking, not governance of conversational or LLM-based systems.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the paper strongly addresses regulated financial compliance, governance, accountability, transparency, privacy, and supervisory review, its technology focus is distributed ledger technology for regulatory reporting workflows. The provided text contains no mention of large language models, generative AI, conversational systems, chatbots, agents, RAG, guardrails, observability of AI outputs, or related conversational governance mechanisms central to the review scope.

appraisal.notes: Short research-in-progress paper using DSR with preliminary artefact requirements and propositions. Governance/accountability themes are present but tied to DLT reporting architecture, not conversational AI governance. Evaluation detail, sample size, and limitations are thin in the excerpt provided.

cerqual.explanation: Internally coherent for DLT compliance reporting, but methodological detail is limited and relevance to conversational LLM governance in regulated settings is very low based on the provided text.

coding.subtheme: Governance and accountability in permissioned DLT reporting artefacts

synthesis.main_claim: DLT may automate key compliance reporting processes through a pull-model that lets regulators access near real-time aggregated exposure data, supported by artefact governance requirements for privacy, delegation, and accountability.
synthesis.contribution: Offers practical DSR insights, six grouped artefact requirements, and four propositions on how DLT can change compliance reporting precision, cost, and supervision in heavily regulated banking contexts.
synthesis.limitations: Marked as research in progress; preliminary findings; further trials and work required; limited evaluation detail in the provided text.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central or supporting evidence on conversational LLM governance; at most marginal contextual background on regulated financial compliance reporting if a broader compliance-governance lens is used.

The increased level of transparency enables more effective and focused supervision and more precise and faster data sharing across the regulated entities
